rules.statement: Every brain must declare capabilities, allowed actions, and blocked actions.
All brains operate in approval-required mode for write-affecting outcomes.
Brain outputs must be reviewable and traceable in reports.
A brain may report execution success only when a real artifact or command result is supported by verifiable evidence.
Test execution requires explicit in-workspace targets, bounded timeouts, shell-disabled invocation, and captured exit evidence.
Engineering intelligence providers may propose bounded artifacts but may not write source, execute commands, perform Git actions, or bypass isolated Tester Brain validation and Founder approval.
Reviewer Brain approval is a technical verdict only and never authorizes source application, commit, push, deploy, or replacement of Founder approval.
Architect Brain plans are read-only and may hand off only allow-listed structured specifications; plans never authorize implementation or external action.
Correction loops are attempt-bounded, stop immediately on Reviewer rejection, accept only allow-listed structured revisions, and never authorize source or Git actions.
Revenue execution missions require an approved GARUDA-deliverable candidate, complete verification, a currently verified commercial capability, and bounded scope before Engineering begins.

Revenue work packages run through the governed Architect, Engineering, Tester, and Reviewer evidence chain; a technical result remains a Founder review checkpoint and never authorizes source, Git, deployment, outreach, contract, spending, payment, or delivery actions.

Founder mission decisions must be bound to verified execution evidence and preserved as immutable hash-chained audit records; a decision changes mission state but grants no external, financial, source, Git, deployment, or delivery authority.

Founder-requested changes may be resubmitted only as a fresh bounded evidence revision; prior scope, evidence, decision, and response identities remain archived, rejected missions stay closed, and total revisions are capped at three.

Deliverable workspace tasks use dependency-aware governed state transitions; completion requires recorded evidence, events remain hash-chained, and workspace progress never authorizes outreach, application, contract, spending, payment, deployment, or delivery.

Autonomous revenue task runs may reconcile only Founder-approved internal work against existing verifiable evidence; retries are capped at three, missing evidence blocks rather than fabricates completion, and no run authorizes external, financial, source, Git, deployment, or delivery action.
Every outreach, application, contract, delivery, deployment, or payment-verification action requires its own evidence-bound Founder decision; mission approval alone grants no external authority.
Approved external actions produce checksum-bound handoff packages only; external completion must be recorded with a verifiable receipt and may never be fabricated or inferred.
GARUDA may claim revenue readiness only from truthful workflow evidence and may claim received income only after explicit payment verification.

Connector dispatch requires an allow-listed action-compatible adapter, an action-specific Founder approval, bound decision and handoff hashes, an idempotency key, and an immutable provider receipt; sandbox validation performs no external side effect.

Revenue acquisition must run continuously on a bounded cadence for internal discovery, source verification, capability matching, grounded drafting, stale-case invalidation, and audit reporting; continuous operation never grants automatic outreach or submission authority.

A revenue source is GARUDA-executable only when its canonical snapshot is fresh, secure, specific direct client work and contains no human identity, CV, profile, interview, employment, or personal-experience gate; recruitment and talent-network listings are not client missions.
Proposal approval and submission recording must revalidate the current source snapshot; a changed, missing, or stale snapshot invalidates the pre-submission case and revokes its handoff.
